full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.: This Civil Petition for leave to appeal has been directed against the judgment and decree dated 24.02.2011 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 230 of 2002 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 04.03.2002 passed by the Joint District Judge 1st Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 136 of 2000 decreeing the suit. 

 4. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties, decreed the suit. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment of the trial court the contesting defendant preferred the First Appeal No. 230 of 2002 before the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing the learned advocates of both the parties and considering the evidence and other facts and circumstances on record, dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and decree of the trial court by the impugned judgment and order. 

 6. Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq, the teamed Senior Advocate has made elaborate submission on behalf of the defendant-petitioner. He has argued to the effect that the High Court Division and also the trial court without proper consideration of the evidence on record decreed the suit, that both the trial court and the appellate court failed to take into consideration that all the witnesses of the plaintiff are interested witnesses and on the basis of evidence of these interested witnesses only the suit for specific performance of contract could not be decreed. That there were so many evidence and facts and circumstances which supported the defence case  strongly and disproved the plaintiff's case but both the courts below have failed to assess these evidence and facts and circumstances properly and consequently failed to come to a correct decision. The learned advocate has argued also that this defendant-petitioner though admitted the signatures in the front page of the stamp paper and cartridge papers of the alleged bainanama to be his own but denied the signatures allegedly put on the back page of this bainapatra allegedly acknowledging receipt of some portion of balance consideration money and in the circumstances the courts below committed gross error in believing those signatures also to be of this defendant without taking any expert's opinion as to genuineness of these signatures. The learned advocate has .argued to the effect also that this defendant petitioner has got no other homestead to live in with his other family members and in the circumstances the courts below has committed great in justice to this defendant in passing the decree for specific performance of contract against him. The learned advocate has argued also that the courts below did not consider that the plaintiff taking unfair advantage and also by fraudulent activities obtained. the alleged bainanama and as such it was not executable at all, that in the circumstances the courts below committed wrong and also illegality in decreeing the suit for specific performance of contract causing great miscarriage of justice. 

 11. Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq, the learned advocate for the petitioner has argued also with much emphasis that this defendant petitioner has got no other homestead to live in with his family members and he will be on the street with his other family members if the decree for specific performance of contract is awarded. It appears that the High Court Division has considered this argument also of the learned advocate for the defendant appellant and has pointed out that the own witness of the defendant has deposed before the court to the effect that this defendant along with his three other brothers had been residing in their ancestral homestead and found that this defendant did not reside in the suit land. The learned advocate for the defendant petitioner has made argument to the effect also that the plaintiff obtained the alleged bainanama taking unfair advantage and also by fraudulent activities and in the circumstances the court should not pass a decree for specific performance of contract, in that the jurisdiction of the court to pass a decree for specific performance of contract is discretionary and the court is not bound to pass such decree in all facts and circumstances. But we are unable to accept this argument also of the learned advocate for the leave petitioner. In this suit for specific performance of contract there is no evidence at all to show that the plaintiff had any undue and unfair advantage or had any fraudulent activities in obtaining the impugned bainanama from the defendant.
